result.cultural_lag_note: Older immigrant couples often wore conservative styles that lagged behind current fashion trends by several years.
result.reasoning_summary: The apparent ages of Rebecca (born ~1865, appearing ~45) and Meyer (born ~1853, appearing ~55-60) strongly point to a date around 1910. This aligns with Rebecca's Edwardian-era dress featuring heavy applique and a high collar, as well as the large oval portrait format which was highly popular among immigrant families in the early 20th century.

location.visual_evidence: Standard studio portrait with no geographic markers; the large oval format was a common fixture in American immigrant homes.
location.biographical_evidence: Genealogical records indicate the family immigrated from Russia/Minsk around 1903-1905. During the estimated photo date range of 1905-1915, census records place their residence in Manhattan (1905, 1910) and later Brooklyn (1915 onwards).

candidates.reasoning: The family's documented residence from 1915 onwards; possible if the photo dates to the later end of the estimated range.
Possible if the portrait was taken just prior to their emigration around 1903, though the style is very characteristic of post-arrival American portraits.
